notes.title: actions/checkout@v4
notes.body:
# Inital Setup

---
touch .github/workflows/ci.yml
This uses: actions/checkout@v4 line tells GitHub Actions to download and run the v4 version of the official checkout action

## ci.yaml

---

name: CI

on: [push]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4 #This uses: actions/checkout@v4 line tells GitHub Actions to download and run the v4 version of the official checkout action.

      - name: List Files
        run: ls -la # The run keyword allows you to execute command-line programs 

---
## index.js File

***echo "console.log('Hello, GitHub Actions!');" > index.js***

notes.title: gitHub Actions Nebula setup v1
notes.body:
# Initial Github Setup

A good setup is:
GitHub Action runs when you push to main.
It verifies nebula_v1/index.html and nebula_v1/fold.js have valid JavaScript.
If the check passes, GitHub triggers Coolify through its webhook—or Coolify’s GitHub App detects the push and redeploys automatically

In your obsidian-vaulTTY repository, create:

*.github/workflows/deploy-nebula.yml*

---
## deploy-nebula.yaml

name: Validate and deploy Nebula

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "nebula_v1/**"
      - ".github/workflows/deploy-nebula.yml"

jobs:
  validate-and-deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Check out code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate Nebula JavaScript
        run: |
          node <<'NODE'
          const fs = require('fs');
          const html = fs.readFileSync('nebula_v1/index.html', 'utf8');

          if (!html.includes('fold.js')) {
            throw new Error('index.html must reference fold.js');
          }

          for (const [, script] of html.matchAll(/<script>([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/g)) {
            new Function(script);
          }

          new Function(fs.readFileSync('nebula_v1/fold.js', 'utf8'));
          console.log('Nebula validation passed.');
          NODE

      - name: Deploy with Coolify
        run: |
          curl --fail --request GET "${{ secrets.COOLIFY_WEBHOOK }}" \
            --header "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.COOLIFY_TOKEN }}"

---
# Github Actions Finial Setup

---
## Create these GitHub repository secrets:

COOLIFY_WEBHOOK — the application’s deploy webhook URL from Coolify.
COOLIFY_TOKEN — an API token created in Coolify

---
## Coolify Webhooks

In Coolify, find your Nebula application’s Webhooks section to get the deployment URL, and create an API token in the Coolify dashboard’s API/token settings

Coolify’s GitHub Actions example uses the same webhook-plus-Bearer-token pattern

---
## Final Push

*git add .github/workflows/deploy-nebula.yaml*
*git commit -m "commit message"*
*git push origin main*

notes.title: Definitions
notes.body:
# Github Actions Trigger Events

Note: GitHub Actions supports many other trigger events. For example:

## pull_request

Triggers when a pull request is opened, synchronized, or closed

## workflow_dispatch

Allows manual triggering from the GitHub Actions tab

## schedule

Runs on a schedule using cron syntax

## release

Triggers when a release is published
And many more events like issues, pull_request_review, etc.

# Github Actions Naming Convention

# Github Actions Jobs

A workflow run is made up of one or more jobs
Jobs run in parallel by default

notes.title: Hello-world.yaml
notes.body:
# hello-world.yml

--touch .github/workflows/hello-world.yml
--ls -lR .github

---
name: Hello World Workflow #This key-value pair assigns a human-readable name to your workflow
on: [push] # The on: [push] configuration tells GitHub Actions to trigger this workflow every time a git push is made to any branch in the repository
jobs: # This job will run on an Ubuntu environment and execute a simple command
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Say Hello
        run: echo "Hello, World!"

---
# Running the Action

*git add .github/workflows/hello-world.yml*
*git commit -m "Add hello world workflow"*
*git push*

---
When you push code, multiple Actions may be triggered if you have multiple workflow files in your repository
Please identify the correct workflow run by checking the workflow name in the left sidebar or using the workflow run list on the right side

---
# Yaml File Breakdown

Let's break down what this does:

a. jobs:: Starts the jobs section
b. build:: The ID of the job
c. runs-on: ubuntu-latest: Specifies the type of machine (runner) to run the job on
d. steps:: A list of tasks to run in the job
e. run: echo "Hello, World!": A shell command to execute

---
# Workflow Breakdown

Click on the workflow run to view the detailed execution logs

You will see:

a. The workflow name: "Hello World Workflow" at the top
b. The job name: "build" in the left sidebar
c. The step execution: Click on the "build" job to expand it, then click on the "Say Hello" step
d. The output: You should see the output Hello, World! displayed in the logs
